newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian industry association welcomes tax changes.
newsitem.headline: Indian industry association welcomes tax changes.

text.p: India's Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) said on Thursday it welcomed modifications in taxes announced by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram while moving a bill to give effect to his budget presented in July.

The association said it welcomed a reduction in capital gains tax on partnership firms which the minister proposed on Wednesday in a revised finance bill which would give effect to the 1996/97 (April-March) budget.
It also approved of his proposal to exempt income earned by companies located in officially declared backward areas from a minimum corporate tax he proposed in July.

"The exclusion of the backward areas from the purview of minimum alternative tax (MAT) will help increase the investment in backward areas and promote balanced regional development," the statement said.

But the association added it was not satisfied with what it called a high excise duty of 15 percent on the steel industry and said it was disappointed that there was no customs duty relief for textile machinery.
